newsitem.title: UK: British Gas takes pause in take-or-pay talks.
newsitem.headline: British Gas takes pause in take-or-pay talks.

text.p: British Gas said it has put further renegotiations of its crippling take-or-pay contracts on hold for the time being to evaluate its achievements so far ahead of the company's demerger next month.

"We have done some deals, which have made an important contribution to solving the overall problem, and there is still some way to go, but we now want to pause for a while and take stock," a British Gas spokeswoman said on Monday.
The take-or-pay contracts oblige British Gas to buy fixed amounts of gas from North Sea gas producers at set prices even if it cannot find a market to sell it on.

The contracts, mostly signed before British Gas' privatisaton in 1986, became a millstone as the utility lost a lot of clients to new competitors when the market for large industrial gas users was opened up in the early 1990s.
British Gas last month announced it had successfully renegotiated take-or-pay contracts with one of its own units, British Petroleum and Mobil.
British Gas was given an unspecified amount in cash for sweetening the supply deal, while Mobil received interests in and around the Beryl gas field.

British Gas said in December it would also use its Morecambe Bay field to help solve the take-or-pay problem, but it declined to say whether this meant selling the field in one go to a single supplier or in bits and pieces to several producers.
Morecambe Bay, located off the coast of north west England, will be the main asset of Centrica, British Gas' supply arm which will be floated off in February.
"It is an important supply element to Centrica, but it is also an important asset in terms of ultimate resolution of the take-or-pay problem," the British Gas spokeswoman said.
"What part it will play will obviously be the subject of negotiations," she added.

In a recent note, Merrill Lynch valued Morecambe Bay at 1.45 billion stg, while the broker estimated that solving the remaining take-or-pay problem would cost Centrica between 1.1 and 1.6 billion stg.
After the deals with Mobil and BP, British Gas said it had solved 20 percent of the total problem.
